details.presidential_2016: Clinton 65,853,514 (48.18%) minus Trump 62,984,828 (46.09%) of 136,669,276 total votes = +2.099. FEC, Federal Elections 2016, 2016 Presidential Popular Vote Summary (p. 5): https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/federalelections2016.pdf . Saved as raw/fec-federalelections2016.pdf
details.generic_ballot_2018: FiveThirtyEight generic-ballot average, 'All polls', 2018-11-06 (Election Day): Democrats 50.65668, Republicans 42.04514 = +8.612 (displayed rounded as 50.7 to 42.0, i.e. D+8.7). Read from the page's embedded 'var generic' series in the Wayback Machine capture of 2018-11-06 21:01 UTC (page stamp 'UPDATED Nov. 6, 2018 at 9:29 AM', before any polls closed): https://web.archive.org/web/20181106210114id_/https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/congress-generic-ballot-polls/ . The 538 page was free (not paywalled). Saved as raw/538-generic-ballot-page-wayback-20181106210114.html. The 2018-11-06 12:42 UTC capture (update 12:29 AM) showed 50.58152 to 42.0419 = +8.540 for the same date; the 9:29 AM update is used as the last pre-election number. Unlike the 2022 sibling, this is a pre-election capture, not a post-election file.

details.congressional_2018: 50 states only: D 61,061,657 (53.202%), R 50,922,621 (44.368%), other 2,789,841, total 114,774,119 = +8.834. Derived from the FEC general-election table '2018 Votes Cast for the U.S. House of Representatives by Party' (Federal Elections 2018, p. 9) by removing the AS, DC, GU, MP and VI delegate rows. The FEC total including delegates (D 61,296,952, R 50,960,112, other 2,820,406) gives +8.983. FEC: https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/federalelections2018.pdf , saved as raw/fec-federalelections2018.pdf
details.congressional_2018_clerk: Clerk of the House, Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 6, 2018, national recapitulation (50 states): D 60,319,623, R 50,467,181, total 114,016,831 = +8.641. Lower than the FEC figure partly because the Clerk credits fusion-line votes (NY Working Families, Independence, etc.) to those parties rather than to the D/R candidate, (NY D 3,760,566 Clerk vs 3,899,563 FEC), and some state totals differ for reasons not traced here (e.g. PA D 2,712,665 Clerk vs 3,016,286 FEC). The FEC figure is the headline value because the district rows sum fusion lines to the candidate, as the 2022 sibling did. Source: https://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/2018election/ (serves the PDF), saved as raw/clerk-statistics-2018-election.pdf
